task: B-0 fallback: alternatives to dictionary pruning for on-device Japanese G2P on ESP32-S3

how_measured.reference: pyopenjtalk 0.4.1-post8 pinned to OPEN_JTALK_DICT_DIR=$PP/build/share/open_jtalk/dic (NAIST-JDIC, lexsize 788,923). phoneme seq = pyopenjtalk.g2p(); phoneme+accent seq = piper_plus_g2p.japanese.JapanesePhonemizer.phonemize() (the canonical piper-plus JA path, tokens include the accent marks [ ] # _ and the ? EOS family).

metrics.phoneme_sentence_exact_pct: % of sentences whose phoneme sequence is identical to the full-dictionary reference
metrics.phoneme_plus_accent_sentence_exact_pct: same but on the JapanesePhonemizer token stream, which carries the accent marks
metrics.accent_structure_sentence_exact_pct: only the (mark, mora-index) sequence for [ ] # _ compared; insensitive to vowel devoicing

how_measured.important: All 'agreement' numbers are agreement WITH THE FULL 103 MB DICTIONARY, not correctness. The full dictionary's own misreadings are invisible to this measurement.

baseline_pruning_with_accent.note: Re-measured because the earlier pruning run only compared PHONEMES. Ranking is TRAIN-split frequency only (data/splits/corpus_train.tsv, 20,946 lines); evaluation is on the held-out split. matrix.bin compacted to used context ids (output-invariant).

accuracy.accent: ZERO. The rule table carries no accent information at all.

control_full_dictionary_fed_the_same_kan.meaning: Running the whole 103 MB dictionary on kana input is WORSE than the 1.6 KB rule table for phonemes, and its accent output is 0.47% sentence-exact. Once the input is kana, the dictionary buys nothing for segmental content and cannot recover accent.

option1a_kana_input_rules_only.devoicing_note: 47.27% of held-out sentences differ from the reference ONLY in vowel devoicing (I/U vs i/u). CLAUDE.md's S_ja noise-injection set depends on I and U, so this is not cosmetic.

option1b_kana_keyed_mecab_dict.note: surface := the katakana reading, so the trie alphabet is kana only. 788,923 -> 471,174 entries after collapsing homophones with identical POS/accent; 340,126 distinct readings.
option1b_kana_keyed_mecab_dict.verdict: Strictly dominated. At every footprint the kanji-keyed dictionary gives better accent (e.g. 3.29 MB kanji = 34.24% accent vs 3.58 MB kana = 9.03%), and the kana dict tops out at 20.6% no matter how big it gets.

option1c_minimal_accent_lookup_table.note: NOT a MeCab dictionary. Flat sorted table: kana key -> {accent type u8, mora count u8, chain-rule id u8, POS id u8} + 3 B binary-search offset per key. This is the cheapest possible 'accent dictionary'.
option1c_minimal_accent_lookup_table.verdict: Storage is cheap (0.68 MB for 30k readings) but unusable on its own: the measured bottleneck is morphological segmentation + accent-phrase chaining, not the lexicon. See option1b levels, which give this table the best possible segmenter and still top out at 20.6% sentence accent accuracy.

audio_comparison.method: pyopenjtalk.tts() HTS mei_normal used as a speaking-rate proxy; its 3.95 s mean on 300 held-out sentences matches the teacher's measured 3.96 s/sentence (plan doc line 37)

numeric_slots.note: 41.4 KiB gives correct readings AND correct accent for every 0-100 x 24-counter combination, including the irregular ones. Alternatively the OpenJTalk digit/counter rule tables are 9,016 B of string data and generate these compositionally.

option3_hybrid_freq_dict_plus_kana_fallb.finding: This is not an extra mechanism: MeCab + unk.dic already IS the hybrid. char.bin routes OOV runs by character class, so an OOV kana word gets read correctly by rule while accent is lost.

measured_oov_behaviour.why this matters: An out-of-vocabulary kanji word is not mispronounced, it is dropped. The listener gets a grammatically broken sentence with no audible signal that anything was lost.

option3_hybrid_freq_dict_plus_kana_fallb.coverage_note: Vocabulary ranked on the 20,946-line train split, measured on the 2,325-line held-out split and the 183-line embedded set. 30,350 is the ENTIRE distinct-surface vocabulary of the train split.
option3_hybrid_freq_dict_plus_kana_fallb.size_vs_accuracy: Use baseline_pruning_with_accent for the size axis: the hybrid's accuracy curve IS that curve.

option4_host_side_g2p.accuracy: identical to the teacher by construction

link_budget_estimate.method: arithmetic from documented link rates, NOT measured on hardware
link_budget_estimate.Opus 16 kbps audio streaming = 2,000 B/s: exceeds that worst-case BLE 4.2 link by 3x, sustained
link_budget_estimate.conclusion: the phoneme-id wire format is 100-3,000x cheaper than streaming the audio, so on-device synthesis still wins the bandwidth/latency/offline-buffer argument even with host-side G2P

product_argument.holds: Any product where the text originates off-device (phone app, gateway, cloud notification) already has the link that would carry phoneme ids. The paper's own system boundary is the same ('external G2P excluded').
product_argument.breaks: Fully standalone operation where the device composes its own text locally (clock, sensor readings, local state machine) with no companion.
product_argument.but: That standalone case is a CLOSED vocabulary, and option 2 covers it: 20 KiB of rules + 41 KiB of number/counter phonemes + ~40 B per template.

option5_neural_g2p.repo: ayousanz/nn-g2p-jp (private, HF, accessible as ayousanz). sha 807c3a29fd7b0211545a6e80c032e78c3b6eea7f, last modified 2026-02-17
option5_neural_g2p.architecture: Conformer encoder 6 layers d_model=384 nhead=6 ffn=1536 kernel=15, shared Transformer decoder 4 layers with dual heads (phone + prosody), joint CTC. Grapheme vocab 4,857 (kanji included), phone vocab 46, prosody vocab 52.
option5_neural_g2p.output_format_matches_piper_plus: phone vocab is exactly the piper-plus JA set (a o i u k e r N s t m sh n g b d h cl y j ts ch z p w f ky ry gy ny hy by my v py dy fy kw ty gw e: o:) and the prosody vocab is the same ^ $ ? _ # [ ] marks JapanesePhonemizer emits. This is the right output format for the student.

compute_measured.method: summed in_features*out_features over every nn.Linear and in/groups*out*kernel over every nn.Conv1d of the instantiated M9 model, times the measured mean input chars (27.0) and output tokens (64.6). beam=1, one decoder pass.

why_it_does_not_fit.flash: 20.4 MB int8 vs the measured ESP32-S3 dictionary budget of 11.19 MB (16 MB board, OTA 2 slots) from reports/b0_flash_budget.json. Does not fit at all.
why_it_does_not_fit.compute: 626 MMAC/sentence vs the whole saanoTTS student at 45 MMAC/audio-second x 3.95 s = 178 MMAC/sentence. The G2P would be 3.5x the entire TTS.
why_it_does_not_fit.memory_traffic_is_the_real_killer: Autoregressive decoding re-reads the 5.97 MB int8 decoder every output token. 64.6 tokens x 5.97 MB = 386 MB per sentence. ESP32-S3 D-cache is at most 64 KB so there is no reuse. At QIO 80 MHz (4 lines SDR = 40 MB/s) that is 9.7 s per sentence; even from octal PSRAM at ~160 MB/s it is 2.4 s. The estimate is arithmetic from documented clocking, not a hardware measurement, but there are two orders of magnitude of headroom in the conclusion.
why_it_does_not_fit.what_would_fit: To keep G2P under 10% of the student's CPU budget the weight traffic must stay under ~3.5 MB/sentence. That means either a ~50 K-param autoregressive decoder or, far better, a NON-autoregressive model whose weights are read once per sentence: a 1 MB non-AR char->phoneme+prosody model costs 25 ms of flash traffic. No such checkpoint exists in the repo; every ja_* checkpoint there is the same encoder-decoder shape (smallest is ja_small_v2 at 66 MB fp32).

option5_neural_g2p.verdict: Not usable as-is. It is however the correct teacher for a distillation target, because its output alphabet already matches piper-plus and it reaches sentence-level PER 0.28%.
